title: Locking in Reverse of Traversal Order
pattern: Two threads traverse a linked data structure (such as a list or tree) in opposite directions while locking nodes incrementally.
why_bad: The physical traversal direction determines the locking order, leading to a dynamic deadlock cycle when threads traverse and lock in reverse directions.
detection: CFG showing multi-node traversals where the lock acquisition path follows opposite node references across different execution threads.
counterexample: Using hand-over-hand locking where all threads traverse strictly from root/head to leaf/tail.
fix: Enforce a single, consistent traversal direction for all operations that acquire nested locks.
